nodes.name: Unit root L-function of a family of toric exponential sums
nodes.statement:
To solidify concepts, we first consider an example of a unit root $L$-function coming from a family of toric exponential sums. Let $\Psi$ be a nontrivial additive character on $\bb F_q$. Let $f \in \bb F_q[\lambda_1^\pm, \ldots, \lambda_s^\pm, x_1^\pm, \ldots, x_n^\pm]$ be a Laurent polynomial, and consider for each $\bar \lambda \in (\overline{\bb F}_q^\times)^s$ and $m \geq 1$, the exponential sum
\[
S_m(f, \bar \lambda) := \sum_{\bar x \in (\bb F_{q^{m \cdot deg(\bar \lambda)}}^\times)^n} \Psi\circ Tr_{\bb F_{q^{m \cdot deg(\bar \lambda)}} / \bb F_q}(f(\bar \lambda, \bar x)).
\]
Define by $L(f, \bar \lambda, T) := \exp( \sum_{m \geq 1} S_m(f, \bar \lambda) \frac{T^m}{m})$ the associated $L$-function. It is known that $L(f, \bar \lambda, T)^{(-1)^{n+1}}$ is a rational function with a unique $p$-adic unit root, say $\pi_0(\bar \lambda)$, which is also a 1-unit. The unit root $L$-function of this family is defined by
\[
L_\text{unit}(\kappa, T) := \prod_{\bar \lambda \in |\bb G_m^s / \bb F_q |} \frac{1}{1 - \pi_0(\bar \lambda)^\kappa T^{deg(\bar \lambda)}},
\]
where $\kappa$ takes on values in the $p$-adic integers $\bb Z_p$.
nodes.statement_short: Example: the unit root $L$-function built from the unique unit roots $\pi_0(\bar\lambda)$ of a family of toric exponential sums.

nodes.name: Newton polyhedron at infinity
nodes.statement: We define the Newton polyhedron of $\c {A}$ at $\infty$, denoted $\Delta_{\infty}(\c {A})$, to be the convex closure of $\c {A} \cup {0}$ in $\bb {R}^n$.

nodes.name: Every support element lies on the Newton boundary at infinity
nodes.statement: We make the simplifying hypothesis that every element $u \in \c {A}$ lies on the Newton boundary at $\infty$  of $\Delta_{\infty}(\c {A})$, that is, the union of all faces of $\Delta_{\infty}(\c {A})$ which do not contain the origin. In other language this is the same as the hypothesis that $w(u) = 1$ for all $u \in \c {A}$  where $w$ is the usual polyhedral weight defined by $\Delta_{\infty}(\c {A})$ (see the next section for definition).
nodes.statement_short: Every exponent in $\mathcal A$ lies on the Newton boundary at infinity, i.e. has weight $w(u)=1$.

nodes.name: Generic polynomial with x-support A
nodes.statement: The generic polynomial $f$ with  $x$-support equal to $\c {A}$ is given by $f(t, x) = \sum t_u x^u  \in \bb F_q[\{ t_u\}_{u \in \c{A}}, x_1^\pm, \ldots, x_n^\pm]$ where $u$ runs over $ \c {A}$ and $\{t_u\}_{u \in \c {A}}$ are  new variables.
nodes.statement_short: $f(t,x)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal A} t_u x^u$ with each coefficient a new variable $t_u$.

nodes.name: Lower-order deformation P
nodes.statement: Let $P(\lambda, x) \in \bb F_q[\lambda_1^\pm, \ldots, \lambda_s^\pm, x_1^\pm, \ldots, x_n^\pm]$ be such that the monomials $\lambda^{\gamma}x^v$ in the support of $P(\lambda, x)$ all satisfy $0 < w(v) < 1$.
nodes.statement_short: $P(\lambda,x)$ is a Laurent polynomial whose monomials $\lambda^\gamma x^v$ have $x$-weight strictly between 0 and 1.

nodes.name: No constant term in f and P
nodes.statement: It is convenient to assume the origin is not in the set  $\c {A}$ and if  $\lambda^{\gamma}x^v$ is in the support of $P$, then $v \neq 0$ so that neither $f$ nor $P$ have a constant term (with respect to the $x$-variables). This assumption will be made throughout this work.
nodes.statement_short: Neither $f$ nor $P$ has a constant term in the $x$-variables.

nodes.name: Degree of a point t-bar
nodes.statement: Let $\bar t \in (\overline{\bb F}_q^*)^{|\c {A}|}$, and denote by $deg(\bar t) = [\bb F_q(\bar t) : \bb F_q]$ the degree of $\bar t$, where $\bb F_q(\bar t)$ means we adjoin every coordinate of $\bar t$ to $\bb F_q$.

nodes.name: Notation d(t-bar)
nodes.statement: We will often write $d(\bar t)$ for $deg(\bar t)$.

nodes.name: Field size q_t
nodes.statement: For convenience, write $q_{\bar t} := q^{d(\bar t)}$ so that $\bb F_{q_{\bar t}} = \bb F_q(\bar t)$.

nodes.name: Relative degree of lambda-bar and q_{t,lambda}
nodes.statement: Next, let $\bar \lambda \in ({\overline{\bb F}_q}^*)^{s}$. Denote by $deg_{\bar t}(\bar \lambda)$ or $d_{\bar t}(\bar \lambda)$ the degree $[\bb F_{q_{\bar t}}(\bar \lambda) : \bb F_{q_{\bar t}}]$; set $q_{\bar t,\bar \lambda} := q_{\bar t}^{d_{\bar t}(\bar \lambda)}$ and  $\bb F_{q_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}} = \bb F_{q_{\bar t}}(\bar \lambda)$.

nodes.name: Exponential sum S_m(t,lambda) and its L-function
nodes.statement:
For each $m \geq 1$, define the exponential sum
\[
S_m(\bar t, \bar \lambda) := \sum_{\bar x \in (\bb F_{{q^m_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}}}^*)^n}  \Psi \circ Tr_{\bb F_{q_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}^m} / \bb F_q}( G(\bar t, \bar \lambda, \bar x))
\]
and its associated $L$-function
\[
L(\bar t, \bar \lambda, T) := \exp\left( \sum_{m=1}^\infty S_m(\bar t, \bar \lambda) \frac{T^m}{m} \right).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Exponential sum of $G(\bar t,\bar\lambda,x)$ over $(\mathbb F_{q^m_{\bar t,\bar\lambda}}^*)^n$ and the associated $L$-function.

nodes.name: Unique unit root of the fibre L-function
nodes.statement: It is well-known \cite{MR2966711} that $L(\bar t, \bar \lambda, T)^{(-1)^{n+1}}$ has a unique reciprocal $p$-adic unit root $\pi_0(\bar t, \bar \lambda)$, which is a 1-unit.
conclusions: $L(\bar t, \bar \lambda, T)^{(-1)^{n+1}}$ has a unique reciprocal $p$-adic unit root $\pi_0(\bar t, \bar \lambda)$, which is a 1-unit

nodes.name: Unit root L-function
nodes.statement:
Let $\kappa \in \bb {Z}_p$ be a $p$-adic integer.  For each $\bar t$, the unit root $L$-function is defined by
\[
L_{unit}(\kappa, \bar t, T) := \prod_{\bar \lambda \in | \bb G_m^{s} / \bb F_{q_{\bar t}}|} \frac{1}{1 - \pi_0(\bar t, \bar \lambda)^\kappa T^{d_{\bar t}(\bar \lambda)}},
\]
where $\kappa$ takes values in the $p$-adic integers $\bb Z_p$.
nodes.statement_short: Euler product over closed points $\bar\lambda$ of $(1-\pi_0(\bar t,\bar\lambda)^\kappa T^{d_{\bar t}(\bar\lambda)})^{-1}$, $\kappa\in\mathbb Z_p$.

nodes.name: Wan's theorem (Dwork's conjecture)
nodes.statement:
Wan's theorem tells us that this $L$-function is $p$-adic meromorphic and so may be written as a quotient of $p$-adic entire functions:
\[
L_{unit}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} = \frac{\prod_{i=1}^\infty (1 - \alpha_i(\kappa, \bar t) T)}{\prod_{j=1}^\infty (1 - \beta_j(\kappa, \bar t) T)}, \qquad \alpha_i \rightarrow 0, \beta_j \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } i, j \rightarrow \infty.
\]
conclusions: this $L$-function is $p$-adic meromorphic and so may be written as a quotient of $p$-adic entire functions
nodes.statement_short: Unit root $L$-functions are $p$-adic meromorphic: a quotient of two $p$-adic entire functions.

nodes.name: pi with pi^{p-1} = -p
nodes.statement: To state the main result, first denote by $\pi \in \overline{\bb Q}_p$ an element satisfying $\pi^{p-1} = -p$.

nodes.name: Teichmuller lift of coefficients A-hat
nodes.statement: Next, writing $G(t, \lambda, x) = f(t, x) + P(\lambda, x) = \sum t_u x^u + \sum A(\gamma, v) \lambda^\gamma x^v \in \bb F_q[x_1^\pm, \ldots, x_n^\pm, \lambda_1^\pm, \ldots, \lambda_s^\pm, \{ t_u \}_{u \in Supp(f)}]$, let  $\hat A(\gamma, v)$ be the Teichm\"uller lift of $A(\gamma, v)$ in $\bb Q_q$ for each $(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)$.

nodes.name: Total family H(t, Lambda, lambda, x)
nodes.statement:
We now replace every coefficient of $A(\gamma, v)$ or $P(\lambda, x)$ with a new variable $\Lambda$: set $\c P(\Lambda, \lambda. x) := \sum_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)} \Lambda_{\gamma, v} \lambda^\gamma x^v$ and
\[
H(t, \Lambda, \lambda, x) := f(t, x)  +  \c P(\Lambda, \lambda, x).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Replace each coefficient of $P$ by a new variable $\Lambda_{\gamma,v}$ and set $H=f+\mathcal P$.

nodes.name: Coefficients of exp(pi H) converge in the open polydisk
nodes.statement:
Note that the series 
\[
\exp \pi H(t, \Lambda, \lambda, x) ) = \sum_{\gamma \in \bb Z^s, u \in \bb Z^n} K_{\gamma, u}(t, \Lambda) \lambda^{\gamma} x^{u}
\]
is well-defined, and its coefficients $K_{\gamma, u}(t, \Lambda)$ are themselves elements in the power-series ring  $\bb Z_p[\zeta_p][[\{ t_u \}_{u \in \c A}, \{ \Lambda_{\gamma, v} \}_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)}]]$, and so converge in the open polydisk $D(0,1^-)^{|\c A| + |Supp(P)|}$ defined by the inequalities $|t_u|_p < 1$ for all $u \in \c A$ and $| \Lambda_{\gamma, v} | < 1$ for all $(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)$.
conclusions: is well-defined, and its coefficients $K_{\gamma, u}(t, \Lambda)$ are themselves elements in the power-series ring  $\bb Z_p[\zeta_p][[\{ t_u \}_{u \in \c A}, \{ \Lambda_{\gamma, v} \}_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)}]]$
nodes.statement_short: The coefficients $K_{\gamma,u}(t,\Lambda)$ of $\exp\pi H$ are integral power series converging on the open unit polydisk.

nodes.name: Unit root function F(t, Lambda)
nodes.statement: Define $\c F(t, \Lambda) := K_{0,0}(t, \Lambda) / K_{0,0}(t^p, \Lambda^p)$ and set $\c F_m(t, \Lambda) := \prod_{i=0}^{m-1}  \c F(t^{p^i}, \Lambda^{p^i})$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal F=K_{0,0}(t,\Lambda)/K_{0,0}(t^p,\Lambda^p)$ and its Frobenius-iterated products $\mathcal F_m$.

nodes.name: Main Theorem (unit root formula)
nodes.statement: Let $\hat t$ be the Teichm\"uller lift of $\bar t$. The function $\c F(t, \Lambda)$ analytically continues to the closed polydisc $D(0,1^+)^{|\c A| + |Supp(P)|}$ defined by  $|t_u|_p \leq 1$, $u \in \c A$ and $|\Lambda_{\gamma, v}| < 1$, $(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)$. Furthermore, $\c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\hat t, \hat A)^\kappa = \prod_{i=0}^{a d(\bar t)} \c F(\hat t^{p^i}, \hat A^{p^i})^\kappa$ is the unique unit root of $L_{unit}(\kappa, \bar t, T) ^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ at each fiber $\bar t$ and $\kappa \in \bb Z_p$, where $\c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\hat t, \hat A)$ means setting each $t_u = \hat t_u$ and $\Lambda_{\gamma, v} = \hat A(\gamma, v)$.
assumptions: Let $\hat t$ be the Teichm\"uller lift of $\bar t$.
conclusions: The function $\c F(t, \Lambda)$ analytically continues to the closed polydisc $D(0,1^+)^{|\c A| + |Supp(P)|}$

$\c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\hat t, \hat A)^\kappa = \prod_{i=0}^{a d(\bar t)} \c F(\hat t^{p^i}, \hat A^{p^i})^\kappa$ is the unique unit root of $L_{unit}(\kappa, \bar t, T) ^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ at each fiber $\bar t$ and $\kappa \in \bb Z_p$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal F$ continues to the closed polydisk, and $\mathcal F_{ad(\bar t)}(\hat t,\hat A)^\kappa$ is the unique unit root of the unit root $L$-function at each fibre.
nodes.label: T: Main Thm

nodes.name: Comparison with the classical exponential-sum unit root
nodes.statement:
\medskip\noindent {\bf Remark.} It is worthwhile to compare this result to the result in \cite{MR2966711}. To that end, consider the (total) family $H(t, \Lambda, \lambda, x)$ above. For each $\bar t \in (\overline{\bb F}_q^\times)^{|\c A|}$ and $m \geq 1$, define the exponential sum
\[
S_m(H, \bar t) := \sum_{(\bar \lambda, \bar x) \in (\bb F_{q^{m \cdot deg(\bar t)}}^\times)^s \times (\bb F_{q^{m \cdot deg(\bar t)}}^\times)^n} \Psi\circ Tr_{\bb F_{q^{m \cdot deg(\bar t)}} / \bb F_q}(H(\bar t, A, \bar \lambda, \bar x)).
\]
Define by $L(H, \bar t, T) := \exp( \sum_{m \geq 1} S_m(f, \bar \lambda) \frac{T^m}{m})$ the associated $L$-function, a rational function over $\bb Q(\zeta_p)$. By \cite{MR2966711}, $L(H, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+n+1}}$ has a unique $p$-adic unit root given by $\c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\hat t, \hat A)$. Conjecturally this type of relation should hold in greater generality.
nodes.statement_short: For the total family $H$, the classical $L$-function also has unique unit root $\mathcal F_{ad(\bar t)}(\hat t,\hat A)$, by earlier work.

nodes.name: Unique unit root is general over the torus
nodes.statement: \medskip\noindent {\bf Remark.} The existence of a unique $p$-adic unit root is a general result for unit root $L$-functions defined over the torus $\bb G_m^s$. This includes the classical case of $L$-functions over of exponential sums defined over the torus; see \cite[Section 3]{MR3249829} for details.

nodes.name: Unique unit root for normalized ordinary sigma-modules
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be a finite extension field of $\bb Q_p$ with uniformizer $\pi$, ring of integers $R$, and residue field $\bb F_q$. Let $(M, \phi)$ be a $c \cdot \log$-convergent, nuclear $\sigma$-module over $R$, ordinary at slope zero of rank one ($h_0 = 1$) with basis $\{ e_i \}_{i \geq 0}$. Assume further the \emph{normalization condition} $\phi e_0 \equiv e_0 \text{ mod}(\pi)$ and $\phi e_i \equiv 0 \text{ mod}(\pi) \text{ for all } i \geq 1$. With this setup, it follows that the associated unit root $L$-function $L_\text{unit}(\kappa, \phi, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ has a unique $p$-adic unit root (and no unit poles).
assumptions: Let $K$ be a finite extension field of $\bb Q_p$ with uniformizer $\pi$, ring of integers $R$, and residue field $\bb F_q$.
Let $(M, \phi)$ be a $c \cdot \log$-convergent, nuclear $\sigma$-module over $R$, ordinary at slope zero of rank one ($h_0 = 1$) with basis $\{ e_i \}_{i \geq 0}$.
Assume further the \emph{normalization condition} $\phi e_0 \equiv e_0 \text{ mod}(\pi)$ and $\phi e_i \equiv 0 \text{ mod}(\pi) \text{ for all } i \geq 1$.
conclusions: the associated unit root $L$-function $L_\text{unit}(\kappa, \phi, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ has a unique $p$-adic unit root (and no unit poles)
nodes.statement_short: A nuclear $\sigma$-module ordinary of rank one at slope zero satisfying the normalization condition has unit root $L$-function with a unique unit root.

nodes.name: Proof of unique unit root for sigma-modules
nodes.statement: To see this, we first note that by \cite[Lemma 2.1]{MR3249829} and \cite[equation (9)]{MR3249829}, $L_\text{unit}(\kappa, \phi, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} \equiv det(1 - F_{B^{[\kappa]}} T)$ mod $\pi$. Next, it follows from the normalization condition that the matrix $B^{[\kappa]}$ takes the form $\begin{psmallmatrix}1 & 0\\0 &0 \end{psmallmatrix}$ mod $\pi$, and thus $det(1 - F_{B^{[\kappa]}} T) \equiv 1 - T$ mod $\pi$. Hence, the Fredholm determinant $det(1 - F_{B^{[\kappa]}} T)$ has a unique $p$-adic unit root proving the results.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce mod $\pi$: the normalization condition makes $B^{[\kappa]}$ congruent to a rank-one projection, so the Fredholm determinant is $1-T$ mod $\pi$.

nodes.name: Reduce to Fredholm determinant mod pi
nodes.statement: To see this, we first note that by \cite[Lemma 2.1]{MR3249829} and \cite[equation (9)]{MR3249829}, $L_\text{unit}(\kappa, \phi, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} \equiv det(1 - F_{B^{[\kappa]}} T)$ mod $\pi$.
nodes.statement_short: Cite Lemma 2.1 and eq. (9) of earlier work to reduce the $L$-function mod $\pi$ to $det(1-F_{B^{[\kappa]}}T)$.

nodes.name: Normalization gives 1 - T mod pi
nodes.statement: Next, it follows from the normalization condition that the matrix $B^{[\kappa]}$ takes the form $\begin{psmallmatrix}1 & 0\\0 &0 \end{psmallmatrix}$ mod $\pi$, and thus $det(1 - F_{B^{[\kappa]}} T) \equiv 1 - T$ mod $\pi$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalization makes $B^{[\kappa]}$ a rank-one projection mod $\pi$, so the determinant is $1-T$ mod $\pi$.

nodes.name: Conclude unique unit root
nodes.statement: Hence, the Fredholm determinant $det(1 - F_{B^{[\kappa]}} T)$ has a unique $p$-adic unit root proving the results.
nodes.statement_short: Hence a unique unit root.

nodes.name: Cone(f) and monoid M(f)
nodes.statement: Let $Cone(f)$ be the union of all rays emanating from the origin and passing through $\Delta_\infty(f)$, and set $M := M(f) := Cone(f) \cap \bb Z^n$.

nodes.name: Polyhedral weight function w
nodes.statement: We define a weight function $w$ on $M$ as follows. For $u \in M$, let $w(u)$ be the smallest non-negative rational number such that $u \in w(u) \Delta(f)$.
differentia: $w(u)$ be the smallest non-negative rational number such that $u \in w(u) \Delta(f)$

nodes.name: Norm-like properties of the weight function
conclusions: $w(u) = 0 $ if and only if $u = 0$.
$w(c u) = c w(u)$ for every $c \geq 0$.
$w(u + v) \leq w(u) + w(v)$ for every $u, v \in M$, with equality holding if and only if $u$ and $v$ are cofacial.

nodes.name: Lower deformation family G
nodes.statement: Our lower deformation family then is defined by $G(t, \lambda, x) := f(t, x) + P(\lambda, x)$.

nodes.name: Set U and polytope Gamma
nodes.statement:
Set
\begin{equation} U := \left\{ \left( \frac{1}{1 - w(u)} \right) \gamma \in \bb Q^s \mid  (\gamma, u) \in Supp(P) \right\},
\end{equation}
and let $\Gamma := \Delta_\infty(U) \subset \bb R^s$.

nodes.name: Definition of U
nodes.statement: U := \left\{ \left( \frac{1}{1 - w(u)} \right) \gamma \in \bb Q^s \mid  (\gamma, u) \in Supp(P) \right\},
nodes.label: E: RelPolyDef

nodes.name: Monoid M(Gamma) and weight w_Gamma
nodes.statement: In a similar way to the above, define $M(\Gamma) := Cone(\Gamma) \cap \bb Z^s$ with associated polyhedral weight function $w_\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Relative polytope
nodes.statement: We call $\Gamma$ the \emph{relative polytope} of the family $G(x, t)$.

nodes.name: Unramified extension Q_q and a
nodes.statement: Let $\bb Q_q$ be the unramified extension of $\bb Q_p$ of degree $a := [\bb F_q : \bb F_p]$, and denote by $\bb Z_q$ its ring of integers.

nodes.name: Element pi-tilde
nodes.statement: Let $\pi \in \overline{\bb Q}_p$  satisfy $\pi^{p-1} = -p$, and let $\tilde \pi$ be an element which satisfies $ord_p(\tilde \pi) = (p-1) / p^2$.

nodes.name: Field Omega_0
nodes.statement: We may have occasion to work over a purely ramified extension $\Omega_0 = \bb Q_p(\hat \pi)$  of $\bb Q_p$ with uniformizer $\hat \pi$ which contains $\bb Q_p(\zeta_p, \tilde \pi)$ and for which $\tilde \pi$ is an integral power of $\hat \pi.$

nodes.name: Field Omega
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega = \bb Q_q(\hat \pi).$

nodes.name: Ring R
nodes.statement: Denote by $R$ the ring of integers  of $\Omega$, and $R_0$ the ring of integers of $\Omega_0$.

nodes.name: Ring O_0
nodes.statement:
Set
\[
\c O_0 := \left\{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} C(\gamma) \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^\gamma  \mid C(\gamma) \in R, C(\gamma) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } \gamma \rightarrow \infty \right\}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal O_0$: series in $\lambda$ over $M(\Gamma)$ with coefficients $C(\gamma)\tilde\pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma)}$, $C(\gamma)\to0$.

nodes.name: Space C_0(O_0)
nodes.statement:
Define
\[
\c C_0(\c O_0) := \left\{\xi = \sum_{\mu \in M(\bar f)} \xi(\mu) \tilde \pi^{w(\mu)} x^\mu \mid \xi(\mu) \in \c O_0, \xi(\mu) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } \mu \rightarrow \infty \right\},
\]
an $\c O_0$-algebra.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal C_0(\mathcal O_0)$: series $\sum\xi(\mu)\tilde\pi^{w(\mu)}x^\mu$ with $\xi(\mu)\in\mathcal O_0$ tending to 0.

nodes.name: Ring O_{0,q}
nodes.statement:
Define
\begin{equation} \c O_{0, q} := \left\{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} C(\gamma) \lambda^{\gamma} \tilde \pi^{w_{q\Gamma}(\gamma)} \mid C(\gamma) \in R, C(\gamma) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } \gamma \rightarrow \infty \right\}.
\end{equation}
This ring is the same as $\c O_0$ except using a weight function defined by the dilation $q \Gamma$ (that is, $w_{q \Gamma}(\gamma) = w_\Gamma(\gamma) / q$).
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal O_{0,q}$ is $\mathcal O_0$ with the weight of the dilated polytope $q\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Definition of O_{0,q}
nodes.statement: \c O_{0, q} := \left\{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} C(\gamma) \lambda^{\gamma} \tilde \pi^{w_{q\Gamma}(\gamma)} \mid C(\gamma) \in R, C(\gamma) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } \gamma \rightarrow \infty \right\}.
nodes.label: E: 32

nodes.name: Space C_0(O_{0,q})
Definition of C_0(O_{0,q})
nodes.statement: \c C_0(\c O_{0,q}) := \left\{ \sum_{u \in M(f)} \xi_u x^u \tilde \pi^{w(u)} \mid \xi_u \in \c O_{0, q},  \xi_u \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } u \rightarrow \infty \right\}.
nodes.label: E: 33

nodes.name: Dwork splitting function
nodes.statement: Dwork defines a splitting function by $\theta(T) := \exp \pi (T - T^p) = \sum_{i = 0}^\infty \theta_i T^i$.

nodes.name: Estimate for splitting function coefficients
nodes.statement: It is well-known that $ord_p(\theta_i) \geq \frac{(p-1)}{p^2} i$ for all $i \geq 0$.
conclusions: $ord_p(\theta_i) \geq \frac{(p-1)}{p^2} i$ for all $i \geq 0$

nodes.name: Teichmuller lifting G-hat
nodes.statement:
Writing
\begin{align*}
G(\bar t, \lambda, x) &= f(\bar t, x) + P(\lambda, x) \\
&= \sum \bar t_u x^u + \sum \bar A(\gamma, v) \lambda^\gamma x^v \in \bb F_{q_{\bar t}}[x_1^\pm, \ldots, x_n^\pm, \lambda_1^\pm, \ldots, \lambda_s^\pm],
\end{align*}
we let 
\[
\hat G(\hat t, \lambda, x) := \sum \hat t_u x^u + \sum \hat {A}(\gamma, v) \lambda^\gamma x^v \in R[x_1^\pm, \ldots, x_n^\pm, \lambda_1^\pm, \ldots, \lambda_s^\pm]
\]
be the lifting of $G$ by lifting the coefficients $\bar A(\gamma, u)$ and $\bar t$ by Teichm\"uller units.

nodes.name: Dwork Frobenius F and F_m
nodes.statement:
Set 
\begin{equation} F(\hat t, \lambda, x) := \prod_{u \in Supp(f)} \theta(\hat t_u x^u) \cdot \prod_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)} \theta( \hat {A}(\gamma, v) \lambda^\gamma x^v)
\end{equation}
and for any $m \geq 1$,
\begin{equation} F_m(\hat t, \lambda, x) := \prod_{i=0}^{m-1}  F^{\sigma^i}(\hat t, \lambda^{p^i}, x^{p^i}),
\end{equation}
where $\sigma$ is the extension of the usual Frobenius generator of $Gal(\bb Q_q / \bb Q_p)$ to $\Omega$ with $\sigma(\hat\pi)=\hat \pi.$
nodes.statement_short: $F$ is the product of splitting functions over the monomials of the lifted $\hat G$; $F_m$ is its Frobenius-twisted $m$-fold product.

nodes.name: Definition of F
nodes.statement: F(\hat t, \lambda, x) := \prod_{u \in Supp(f)} \theta(\hat t_u x^u) \cdot \prod_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)} \theta( \hat {A}(\gamma, v) \lambda^\gamma x^v)
nodes.label: E: 38a

nodes.name: Definition of F_m
nodes.statement: F_m(\hat t, \lambda, x) := \prod_{i=0}^{m-1}  F^{\sigma^i}(\hat t, \lambda^{p^i}, x^{p^i}),
nodes.label: E: 38b

nodes.name: p-adic estimate for coefficients of F_m
nodes.statement:
Note that if we set $F_m(\hat t, \lambda, x) = \sum_{u \in M(f)} \mathcal{B}^m(u)x^u = \sum_{\gamma \in M_(\Gamma), u \in M(f)} \mathcal{B}^m (\gamma, u) \lambda^{\gamma} x^u ,$ then 
\[
ord_p (\mathcal{B}^m (\gamma, u)) \geq \frac{w_{\Gamma}(\gamma) + w(u)}{p^{m-1}} \cdot \frac{p-1}{p^2}.
\]
conclusions: ord_p (\mathcal{B}^m (\gamma, u)) \geq \frac{w_{\Gamma}(\gamma) + w(u)}{p^{m-1}} \cdot \frac{p-1}{p^2}.
nodes.statement_short: Coefficients $\mathcal B^m(\gamma,u)$ of $F_m$ have valuation at least $(w_\Gamma(\gamma)+w(u))(p-1)/(p^{m+1})$.

nodes.name: Operator psi_x
nodes.statement: Define $\psi_x$ by $\sum C(u) x^u \mapsto \sum C(p u) x^u$.

nodes.name: Dwork operators alpha_m
nodes.statement:
Set
\[
\alpha_1 :=  \sigma^{-1} \circ \psi_x \circ F(\hat t, \lambda, x)
\]
A similar argument to that in \cite{MR3239170} demonstrates that $\alpha_1$ maps $\sigma^{-1}$-semilinearly $\c C_0(\c O_0)$ into $\c C_0( \c O_{0, p})$. Similarly, for $m \geq 1$, if we define
\[
\alpha_m := \sigma^{-m} \circ \psi_x^m \circ F_m(\hat t, \lambda, x),
\]
then $\alpha_m$ maps $\c C_0(\c O_0)$ into $\c C_0(\c O_{0, p^m})$.
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha_m=\sigma^{-m}\circ\psi_x^m\circ F_m$, mapping $\mathcal C_0(\mathcal O_0)$ into $\mathcal C_0(\mathcal O_{0,p^m})$.

nodes.name: Estimate for alpha_m on basis elements
nodes.statement: In particular, $\alpha_m(\tilde{\pi}^{w(v)} x^v) = \sum_{u \in M(f)} \tilde{\pi}^{w(v)-w(u)}\mathcal{B}^m(p^m u -v) \tilde{\pi}^{w(u)} x^u$, with $ord_p(\tilde{\pi}^{w(v)-w(u)}\mathcal{B}^m(p^m u -v)  \geq \frac{(p^m - 1)w(u) + (p^{m-1} -1)w(v)}{p^{m-1}} ord_p( \tilde{\pi})$. Summarizing, we have in $\c C_0(\c O_{0,p^m}),  |\alpha_m(\tilde{\pi}^{w(v)}x^v)| \leq |\tilde{\pi}|^{w(v) \frac{p^{m-1} -1}{p^{m-1}}}$.
conclusions: |\alpha_m(\tilde{\pi}^{w(v)}x^v)| \leq |\tilde{\pi}|^{w(v) \frac{p^{m-1} -1}{p^{m-1}}}
nodes.statement_short: $|\alpha_m(\tilde\pi^{w(v)}x^v)|\le|\tilde\pi|^{w(v)(p^{m-1}-1)/p^{m-1}}$.

nodes.name: Fibre Frobenius alpha_{t,lambda}
nodes.statement:
\bigskip\noindent{\bf Fibers.} Define
\[
\alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda} := \psi_x^{a d(\bar t) d(\bar \lambda)} \circ F_{a d(\bar t) d(\bar \lambda)}(\hat t, \hat \lambda, x),
\]
where $\hat t$ and $\hat \lambda$ are the Teichm\"uller representatives of $\bar t$ and $\bar \lambda$, respectively.

nodes.name: Fibre space C_0(lambda-hat)
nodes.statement: Notice that $\alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}$ is an endomorphism of $\c C_0(\hat \lambda)$, where $\c C_0(\hat \lambda)$ denotes the space obtained from $\c C_0(\c O_0)$ by applying the map on  $\c O_0$  which sends  $\lambda \ \textup{to} \ \hat \lambda.$

nodes.name: Operation delta_q
nodes.statement: To relate the $L$-function $L(\bar t, \bar \lambda, T)$ to the operator $\alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}$ it is convenient to introduce the following operation: for any function $g(T)$, define $g(T)^{\delta_q} := g(T) / g(qT)$.

nodes.name: Dwork's trace formula
nodes.statement:
Dwork's trace formula states
\[
(q_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}^m-1)^n Tr(\alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}^m \mid \c C_0(\hat \lambda)) = \sum_{\bar x \in \left(\bb F_{q_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}^m}^*\right)^n} \Psi \circ Tr_{\bb F_{q_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}^m} / \bb F_q}( G(\bar t, \bar \lambda, \bar x))
\]
Equivalently,
\[
L(\bar t, \bar \lambda, T)^{(-1)^{n+1}} = det(1 - \alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda} T \mid \c C_0(\hat \lambda))^{\delta_{q_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}}^n}.
\]
conclusions: L(\bar t, \bar \lambda, T)^{(-1)^{n+1}} = det(1 - \alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda} T \mid \c C_0(\hat \lambda))^{\delta_{q_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}}^n}.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential sums are traces of iterates of $\alpha_{\bar t,\bar\lambda}$; equivalently the $L$-function is a $\delta$-twisted Fredholm determinant.

nodes.name: Roots pi_i(t, lambda)
nodes.statement: Denote the roots of $det(1 - \alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda} T \mid \c C_0(\hat \lambda) )$ by $\pi_i(\bar t, \bar \lambda)$, and order them such that $ord_p \> \pi_i(\bar t, \bar \lambda) \leq ord_p \> \pi_{i+1}(\bar t, \bar \lambda)$ for $i \geq 0$.

nodes.name: L-functions L^{(m)}
nodes.statement:
For each $m \geq 0$, define
\[
L^{(m)}(\kappa, \bar t, T) := \prod_{\bar \lambda \in | \bb G_m^s / \bb F_{q_{\bar t}}|} \prod (1 - \pi_0(\bar t, \bar \lambda)^{\kappa - r - m} \pi_{i_1}(\bar t, \bar \lambda) \cdots \pi_{i_r}(\bar t, \bar \lambda) \cdot \pi_{j_1}(\bar t, \bar \lambda) \cdots \pi_{j_m}(\bar t, \bar \lambda) T^{deg(\bar \lambda)})^{-1}
\]
where the inner product runs over all $r \geq 0$, $1 \leq i_1 \leq i_2 \leq \cdots$, and $0 \leq j_1 < \cdots < j_m$.
nodes.statement_short: $L^{(m)}$: Euler product of $Sym^{\kappa-m}\otimes\wedge^m$ combinations of the roots $\pi_i$ normalized by $\pi_0^{\kappa-r-m}$.

nodes.name: Decomposition of the unit root L-function (Lemma 2.1 of [MR3249829])
nodes.statement:
L_\text{unit}( \kappa, \bar t, T) = \prod_{i = 0}^\infty L^{(i)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{i-1} (i-1)}
=L^{(0)}(\kappa,\bar t, T) \prod_{i \geq 2}L^{(i)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{i-1}(i-1)}.
conclusions: L_\text{unit}( \kappa, \bar t, T) = \prod_{i = 0}^\infty L^{(i)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{i-1} (i-1)}
nodes.statement_short: $L_{unit}$ is an alternating product of powers of the $L^{(i)}$, $i\ge0$.
nodes.label: E: Adams

nodes.name: Formal power series ring S(lambda-hat)
nodes.statement: Denote by $\c S(\hat \lambda) := R[\hat \lambda][[ \{e_u\}_{u \in M \setminus \{0\}}]]$ the formal power series ring over $R[\hat \lambda]$ in the variables $\{e_u \}_{u \in M \setminus \{0\}}$ which are formal symbols indexed by the $M \setminus \{0\}$.

nodes.name: Monomials e_u
nodes.statement: It is convenient to write the monomials of degree $r$ in the variables $\{ e_u \}$ using the notation $e_{\b u} := e_{u_1} \cdots e_{u_r}$, where $u_1, \ldots, u_r \in M(f) \setminus \{0\}$ for  $r \geq 0$.

nodes.name: Weight of monomials w(u)
nodes.statement: We extend the weight function $w$ to such monomials by defining, for $e_{\b u} := e_{u_1} \cdots e_{u_r}$, the weight $w(\b u) := w(u_1) + \cdots + w(u_r)$.

nodes.name: Index set S(M)
nodes.statement: Denote by $\c S(M)$ the set of all indices $\b u$ corresponding to monomials $e_{\b u}$.

nodes.name: Embedding Upsilon
nodes.statement:
We may identify $\c C_0(\hat \lambda)$ as an $R[\hat \lambda]$-submodule  of $\c S(\hat \lambda)$ by defining an $R[\hat \lambda]$-linear map 
\[
\Upsilon: \c C_0(\hat \lambda) \rightarrow \c S(\hat \lambda) \qquad  \text{via} \qquad  \sum_{u \in M(f)} \xi_u \tilde \pi^{w(u)} x^u \longmapsto \xi_0 + \sum_{u \in M(f)\setminus \{0\}} \xi_u e_u.
\]

nodes.name: Banach algebra S_0(lambda-hat)
nodes.statement:
Define the $R[\hat \lambda]$-subalgebra of $\c S(\hat \lambda) $
\[
\c S_0(\hat \lambda) := \left\{ \xi = \sum_{\b u \in \c S(M)} \xi(\b u) e_{\b u} \mid \xi(\b u) \in R[\hat \lambda], \xi(\b u) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } w(\b u) \rightarrow \infty \right\}.
\]

nodes.name: Infinite symmetric power operator [alpha_{t,lambda}]_kappa
nodes.statement:
Define $[\alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}]_\kappa: \c S_0(\hat \lambda) \rightarrow \c S_0(\hat \lambda)$ by extending linearly over $R[\hat \lambda]$ the action on monomials of degree $r$ 
\[
[\alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}]_\kappa( e_{u_1} \cdots e_{u_r} ) := (\Upsilon \circ \alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda} (1) )^{\kappa - r} (\Upsilon \circ \alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda} ( \tilde \pi^{w(u_1)} x^{u_1})) \cdots ( \Upsilon \circ \alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda} (\tilde \pi^{w(u_r)} x^{u_r})).
\]
nodes.statement_short: $[\alpha]_\kappa$ sends $e_{u_1}\cdots e_{u_r}$ to $(\Upsilon\alpha(1))^{\kappa-r}\prod_i\Upsilon\alpha(\tilde\pi^{w(u_i)}x^{u_i})$.

nodes.name: Fredholm determinant of [alpha_{t,lambda}]_kappa
nodes.statement:
By a similar argument to \cite[Corollary 2.4, part 2]{MR3249829}, 
\[
det(1 - [\alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}]_\kappa T \mid \c S_0(\hat \lambda) ) = \prod_{r = 0}^\infty \prod \left(1 - \pi_0(\bar t, \bar \lambda)^{\kappa - r} \pi_{i_1}(\bar t, \bar \lambda) \cdots \pi_{i_r}(\bar t, \bar \lambda)  T \right)
\]
where the inner product runs over all multisets $\{i_1, \ldots, i_r\}$ of positive integers of cardinality $r$ satisfying $1 \leq i_1 \leq i_2 \leq \cdots$.
conclusions: det(1 - [\alpha_{\bar t, \bar \lambda}]_\kappa T \mid \c S_0(\hat \lambda) ) = \prod_{r = 0}^\infty \prod \left(1 - \pi_0(\bar t, \bar \lambda)^{\kappa - r} \pi_{i_1}(\bar t, \bar \lambda) \cdots \pi_{i_r}(\bar t, \bar \lambda)  T \right)
nodes.statement_short: The Fredholm determinant of $[\alpha_{\bar t,\bar\lambda}]_\kappa$ is the product over multisets of $(1-\pi_0^{\kappa-r}\pi_{i_1}\cdots\pi_{i_r}T)$.

nodes.name: Power series ring S(O_0)
nodes.statement: Denote by $\c S(\c O_0) := \c O_0[[ \{ e_u \}_{u \in M \setminus \{0\}}]]$, the formal power series ring supported by the monomials $\c S(M)$, with coefficients in the ring $\c O_0$.

nodes.name: Banach algebras S_0(O_0) and S_0(O_{0,q})
nodes.statement:
Define the $p$-adic Banach algebra over $\c O_0$,
\begin{align*}
\c S_0(\c O_0) :&= \{ \xi =  \sum_{\b u \in \c S(M)} \xi(\b u) e_{\b u} \mid \xi(\b u) \in \c O_0, \xi(\b u) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } w(\b u) \rightarrow \infty \} \\
&= \{ \xi = \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in \c S(M)} C(\gamma, \b u) \tilde \pi^{w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)} \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u} \mid C(\gamma, \b u) \in R, C(\gamma, \b u) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w(\b u) \rightarrow \infty \},
\end{align*}
and similarly, for any $q = p^a$ an arbitrary power of $p$ (including the case when $a = 0$),
\[
\c S_0(\c O_{0, q}) := \{ \sum_{\b u \in \c S(M)} \xi(\b u) e_{\b u} \mid \xi(\b u) \in \c O_{0, q}, \xi(\b u) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } w(\b u) \rightarrow \infty \}.
\]

nodes.name: Family operator [alpha_m]_kappa
nodes.statement:
We define a map $[\alpha_m]_\kappa : \c S_0(\c O_0) \rightarrow \c S_0(\c O_{0, p^m})$ as follows. On a basis element $e_{\b u} = e_{u_1} \cdots e_{u_r}$ with $r > 0$ and $0 < u_1 \leq \cdots \leq u_r$, 
\[
[\alpha_m](e_{\b u}) := [\alpha_m]_\kappa( e_{u_1} \cdots e_{u_r} ) := (\Upsilon \circ \alpha_m( 1 ))^{\kappa - r} (\Upsilon \circ \alpha_m (\tilde \pi^{w(u_1)} x^{u_1}) ) \cdots (\Upsilon \circ \alpha_m (\tilde \pi^{w(u_r)} x^{u_r})).
\]
If $r = 0$, 
\[
[\alpha_m]_\kappa(1) := \Upsilon( \alpha_m(1))^\kappa.
\]

nodes.name: Expansion of F_m (splitting)
nodes.statement: F_m(\hat t, \lambda, x) = \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), v \in M(f)} B(\gamma, v) \tilde \pi^{( w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w(v)) / p^{m-1}} \lambda^\gamma x^v,
nodes.label: E: splitting

nodes.name: Upsilon estimate
nodes.statement: | \Upsilon( \alpha_m( \tilde \pi^{w(u)} x^u) ) | \leq | \tilde \pi |^{ \frac{p^{m-1}-1}{p^{m-1}} w(u)}
nodes.label: E: upsilon estimate

nodes.name: Operator psi_lambda
nodes.statement:
The $R$-linear map $\psi_\lambda: \c S_0(\c O_{0, p}) \rightarrow \c S_0(\c O_0)$ is defined by 
\[
\psi_\lambda: \quad \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in \c S(M)} A(\gamma, \b u)  \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u} \longmapsto \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in \c S(M)} A(p \gamma, \b u)  \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}
\]

nodes.name: Operator beta_{kappa,t}
nodes.statement:
Then 
\[
\beta_{\kappa, \bar t} := \psi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)} \circ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa: \c S_0(\c O_0) \rightarrow \c S_0(\c O_0)
\]
is a completely continuous operator (over $R$).

nodes.name: Basis B
nodes.statement: Set $\c B := \{ e_{\b u} \mid  \b u \in \c S(M)\}$.

nodes.name: Matrix B^{[kappa]}_t(lambda)
nodes.statement: Let $B^{[\kappa]}_{\bar t}(\lambda)$ be the matrix of $[\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa$ with respect to $\c B$, the basis of $\c S_0(\c O_0)$ over $\c O_0$ (as well as $\c S_0(\c O_{0, p^m})$ over $\c O_{0, p^m}$).

nodes.name: Matrix F_{B^{[kappa]}}
nodes.statement: We define the matrix $F_{B^{[\kappa]}_{\bar t}} := (b_{q_{\bar t} \gamma - \mu}^{[\kappa]} )_{(\gamma, \mu)}$ indexed by $\gamma, \mu \in M(\Gamma)$, and we set $b_{q_{\bar t} \gamma - \mu}^{[\kappa]} := 0$ if $q_{\bar t} \gamma - \mu \not\in M(\Gamma)$.

nodes.name: F_B is the matrix of beta (from [MR3239170])
nodes.statement: As we showed in \cite[\S 2.3]{MR3239170}, $F_{B^{[\kappa]}_{\bar t}}$ is the matrix of the completely continuous operator $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}$, and as such it has a well-defined Fredholm determinant.
conclusions: $F_{B^{[\kappa]}_{\bar t}}$ is the matrix of the completely continuous operator $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}$, and as such it has a well-defined Fredholm determinant

nodes.name: L^{(0)} as Fredholm determinant of beta
nodes.statement: L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T)^{\delta_{q_{\bar t}}^{s}}.
nodes.label: E: A

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement:
Since the Fredholm determinant $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T)$ is $p$-adically entire, this demonstrates the meromorphic continuation of $L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)$.  Since the matrix of $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}$ shows that $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T)$ has a unique unit root,  it follows  that $L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ has a unique unit root equal in fact to the unique unit root of $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T).$

 In a similar way, define on the space $\c S_0(\c O_0) \otimes \wedge^m \c C_0(\c O_0)$, the operator $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^{(m)} := \psi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)} \circ ([\alpha_{a d(\bar t})]_{\kappa-m} \otimes \wedge^m \alpha_{a d(\bar t)})$. Then
\[
L^{(m)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^{(m)} T)^{\delta_{q_{\bar t}}^{s}}.
\]
In particular, for $m \geq 2$, due to the wedge product,  $L^{(m)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ has no zeros or poles on the closed unit disk. Hence, by (\ref{E: Adams}), we have:
nodes.statement_short: $L^{(0)}$ has a unique unit root via the Fredholm determinant of $\beta$; for $m\ge2$ the wedge factor kills unit zeros of $L^{(m)}$; conclude by the decomposition (6).

nodes.name: Meromorphic continuation of L^{(0)}
nodes.statement: Since the Fredholm determinant $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T)$ is $p$-adically entire, this demonstrates the meromorphic continuation of $L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Entireness of $det(1-\beta T)$ gives meromorphy of $L^{(0)}$.

nodes.name: Unique unit root of L^{(0)}
nodes.statement: Since the matrix of $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}$ shows that $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T)$ has a unique unit root,  it follows  that $L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ has a unique unit root equal in fact to the unique unit root of $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T).$
nodes.statement_short: The matrix of $\beta$ shows a unique unit root, hence so does $L^{(0)}$.

nodes.name: Operators beta^{(m)} for L^{(m)}
nodes.statement:
In a similar way, define on the space $\c S_0(\c O_0) \otimes \wedge^m \c C_0(\c O_0)$, the operator $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^{(m)} := \psi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)} \circ ([\alpha_{a d(\bar t})]_{\kappa-m} \otimes \wedge^m \alpha_{a d(\bar t)})$. Then
\[
L^{(m)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^{(m)} T)^{\delta_{q_{\bar t}}^{s}}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Define $\beta^{(m)}$ on $\mathcal S_0\otimes\wedge^m\mathcal C_0$ and express $L^{(m)}$ via its determinant.

nodes.name: No unit zeros for m >= 2
nodes.statement: In particular, for $m \geq 2$, due to the wedge product,  $L^{(m)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ has no zeros or poles on the closed unit disk.
nodes.statement_short: The wedge product forces divisibility, so $L^{(m)}$, $m\ge2$, has no unit zeros or poles.

nodes.name: Conclude via decomposition (6)
nodes.statement: Hence, by (\ref{E: Adams}), we have:
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the decomposition (6).

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1 (unique unit root)
nodes.statement: $L_\text{unit}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s + 1}}$ has a unique $p$-adic unit root which in fact is the unique unit root of $L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$.
conclusions: $L_\text{unit}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s + 1}}$ has a unique $p$-adic unit root which in fact is the unique unit root of $L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$
nodes.statement_short: The unit root $L$-function has a unique unit root, equal to that of $L^{(0)}$.
nodes.label: T: unique unit

nodes.name: Dual space C_0^*(O_{0,q})
nodes.statement:
For $q = p^a$ an arbitrary power of $p$ (including the case $a = 0$) define the $\c O_{0, q}$-module
\[
\c C_0^*(\c O_{0, q}) := \left\{ \sum_{u \in M(f)} \xi(u) \tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u} \mid \xi(u) \in {\c O}_{0, q}  \right\},
\]
equipped with the sup-norm on the set of coefficients $\{ \xi(u) \}_{u \in M(f)}$.

nodes.name: Projection pr_{M(f)} and dual Frobenius alpha_m^*
nodes.statement:
Define the projection (or truncation) map 
\[
\text{pr}_{M(f)}: \quad \sum_{u \in \bb Z^n} A(u) x^{-u} \longmapsto \sum_{u \in M(f)} A(u) x^{-u}.
\]
For each $m \geq 1$, define
\[
\alpha_m^* := \text{pr}_{M(f)} \circ F_m(\hat t, \lambda, x) \circ \Phi_x^m \circ \sigma^m,
\]
where $\sigma \in Gal(\Omega/\Omega_0)$ acts on coefficients (as mentioned above), and $\Phi_x$ acts on monomials by $\Phi_x(x^u) := x^{p u}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha_m^*=\mathrm{pr}_{M(f)}\circ F_m\circ\Phi_x^m\circ\sigma^m$, with $\mathrm{pr}_{M(f)}$ truncation to $M(f)$ and $\Phi_x: x^u\mapsto x^{pu}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 (dual Frobenius estimates)
nodes.statement:
$\alpha_m^*: \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m}) \rightarrow \c C_0^*({\c O}_{0, p^m})$ is a linear map over $\c O_{0, p^m}$. Furthermore, writing 
\[
\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}) = \sum_{z \in M(f)} C_v(z) \tilde \pi^{-w(z)} x^{-z}
\]
with $C_v(z) \in \c O_{0, p^m}$, then $C_v(z) \rightarrow 0$ in $\c O_{0, p^m}$ as $w(v) \rightarrow \infty$. In addition, we may write $\alpha_m^*(1) = 1 + \eta_m^*(\lambda, x),$  with $\eta_m^*(\lambda, x) \in \c C^*_0(\c O_{0,p^m})$ having $|\eta_m^*| \leq |\tilde{\pi}|.$
conclusions: $\alpha_m^*: \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m}) \rightarrow \c C_0^*({\c O}_{0, p^m})$ is a linear map over $\c O_{0, p^m}$.
$C_v(z) \rightarrow 0$ in $\c O_{0, p^m}$ as $w(v) \rightarrow \infty$
we may write $\alpha_m^*(1) = 1 + \eta_m^*(\lambda, x),$  with $\eta_m^*(\lambda, x) \in \c C^*_0(\c O_{0,p^m})$ having $|\eta_m^*| \leq |\tilde{\pi}|.$
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha_m^*$ is an $\mathcal O_{0,p^m}$-linear endomorphism of the dual space with decaying matrix coefficients and $\alpha_m^*(1)\equiv1$ mod $\tilde\pi$.
nodes.label: L: better conv

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement:
We consider $\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v})$ with $v \in M(f)$. Using (\ref{E: splitting}), we may write this as
\[
\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}) = \sum_{z \in M(f), \gamma \in M(\Gamma)} B(\gamma, -z + p^m v) \tilde \pi^{w(\gamma) / p^{m-1}} \lambda^\gamma \cdot \tilde \pi^{w(z) + ( w(-z + p^m v) / p^{m-1})} \cdot \tilde \pi^{-w(z)} x^{-z}.
\]
Since 
\[
-w(v) + w(z) + \frac{1}{p^{m-1}} w(-z + p^m v) \geq \frac{p^{m-1} - 1}{p^{m-1}} w(z) + p w(v),
\]
we see that 
\begin{equation} \alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}) = \tilde \pi^{(p-1) w(v)} \zeta_v^*(\lambda),
\end{equation}
where $\zeta_v^*(\lambda,x) \in \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m})$. 

If $\xi^* \in \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m})$ with $\xi^* = \sum_{v \in M(f)} A_v(\lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}$, then 
\[
\alpha_m^*( \xi^*) = \sum_{v \in M(f)} \tilde \pi^{(p-1)w(v)} A_v(\lambda) \eta_v^*(\lambda) \in \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m}).
\]
Finally, note that by the above,
\[
\alpha_m^*(1) = 1 + \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)-0} B(\gamma,0) \tilde{\pi} ^{w(\gamma)/p^{m-1}} \lambda^{\gamma} + \sum_{z \in M(f)-0, \gamma \in M(\Gamma)} B(\gamma, -z) \tilde{\pi}^{w(z) + (w(-z)/p^{m-1})}(\tilde{\pi}^{w(\gamma)/p^{m-1}} \lambda^{\gamma}) (\tilde{\pi}^{w(-z)} x^{-z}).
\] 
This proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\alpha_m^*$ on basis monomials via the splitting (7) and bound exponents of $\tilde\pi$ using the weight inequalities.

nodes.name: Expand alpha_m^* via splitting
nodes.statement:
We consider $\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v})$ with $v \in M(f)$. Using (\ref{E: splitting}), we may write this as
\[
\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}) = \sum_{z \in M(f), \gamma \in M(\Gamma)} B(\gamma, -z + p^m v) \tilde \pi^{w(\gamma) / p^{m-1}} \lambda^\gamma \cdot \tilde \pi^{w(z) + ( w(-z + p^m v) / p^{m-1})} \cdot \tilde \pi^{-w(z)} x^{-z}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Write $\alpha_m^*$ on a basis monomial using expansion (7).

nodes.name: Weight inequality gives estimate (10)
nodes.statement:
Since 
\[
-w(v) + w(z) + \frac{1}{p^{m-1}} w(-z + p^m v) \geq \frac{p^{m-1} - 1}{p^{m-1}} w(z) + p w(v),
\]
we see that 
\begin{equation} \alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}) = \tilde \pi^{(p-1) w(v)} \zeta_v^*(\lambda),
\end{equation}
where $\zeta_v^*(\lambda,x) \in \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m})$.
nodes.statement_short: Weight inequality yields $\alpha_m^*(E_v^*)=\tilde\pi^{(p-1)w(v)}\zeta_v^*$.

nodes.name: Action on general elements
nodes.statement:
If $\xi^* \in \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m})$ with $\xi^* = \sum_{v \in M(f)} A_v(\lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}$, then 
\[
\alpha_m^*( \xi^*) = \sum_{v \in M(f)} \tilde \pi^{(p-1)w(v)} A_v(\lambda) \eta_v^*(\lambda) \in \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m}).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Extend linearly to general $\xi^*$, staying in the dual space.

nodes.name: Form of alpha_m^*(1)
nodes.statement:
Finally, note that by the above,
\[
\alpha_m^*(1) = 1 + \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)-0} B(\gamma,0) \tilde{\pi} ^{w(\gamma)/p^{m-1}} \lambda^{\gamma} + \sum_{z \in M(f)-0, \gamma \in M(\Gamma)} B(\gamma, -z) \tilde{\pi}^{w(z) + (w(-z)/p^{m-1})}(\tilde{\pi}^{w(\gamma)/p^{m-1}} \lambda^{\gamma}) (\tilde{\pi}^{w(-z)} x^{-z}).
\] 
This proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\alpha_m^*(1)=1+O(\tilde\pi)$, completing the lemma.

nodes.name: Estimate (10) for alpha_m^*
nodes.statement: \alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}) = \tilde \pi^{(p-1) w(v)} \zeta_v^*(\lambda),
nodes.label: E: an estimate

nodes.name: Ring A_0
nodes.statement:
Define
\[
\c A_0 := \left\{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} A(\gamma) \lambda^\gamma : A(\gamma) \in R \text{ and } A(\gamma) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } w(\gamma) \rightarrow \infty \right\}.
\]

nodes.name: Pairing between C_0 and C_0^*
nodes.statement:
For $q_1$ and $q_2$ any two powers of the prime $p$, define a pairing $(\cdot, \cdot): \c C_0(\c O_{0, q_1}) \times \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, q_2}) \rightarrow \c A_0$ by
\[
(\xi, \xi^*) := \text{ the constant term with respect to $x$ of the product $\xi \cdot \xi^*$.}
\]
This product is well-defined since if $\{\eta_1(v)\}_{v \in M(\Gamma)} \subset \c O_{0, q_1}$ with $\eta_1(v) \rightarrow 0$ as $w(v) \rightarrow \infty$, and $\{ \eta_2(v) \}_{v \in M(\Gamma)} \subset \c O_{0, q_2}$, then $\sum_{v \in M(\Gamma)} \eta_1(v) \eta_2(v) \in \c A_0$.
nodes.statement_short: $(\xi,\xi^*)$ is the constant term in $x$ of $\xi\xi^*$, valued in $\mathcal A_0$.

nodes.name: Adjointness of psi_x F_m and pr F_m Phi_x
nodes.statement: ( (\psi_x^m \circ F_m) \xi, \xi^*) = ( F_m \xi, \Phi_x^m \xi^*) = (\xi, (\text{pr}_{M(f)} \circ F_m \circ \Phi_x^m)( \xi^*)).
nodes.label: E: pairing1

nodes.name: Basis E_u and symmetric-power basis E_u-bold
nodes.statement:
We will for convenience of notation write the ``basis'' as $\{ E_u := \tilde \pi^{w(u)} x^u \mid u \in M(f) \}$, and the $k$-th symmetric power of the basis as
\[
E_{\b u} := E_{u_{j_1}} E_{u_{j_2}} \cdots E_{u_{j_k}}, \qquad 0 \leq j_1 \leq j_2 \leq \cdots \leq j_k,
\] 
where $\b u$ runs over multisets of indices of cardinality $k$, say
\[
\{ \b u = (u_{j_1}, u_{j_2}, \ldots, u_{j_k}) \mid 0 \leq u_{j_1} \leq u_{j_2} \leq \cdots \leq u_{j_k} \}.
\]

nodes.name: Symmetric powers Sym^k C_0(O_0) and Sym^k alpha_m
nodes.statement:
Defining
\[
Sym^k_{\c O_0} \c C_0(\c O_0) := \left\{ \xi = \sum_{|\b u| = k} \xi_{\b u}(\lambda) E_{\b u} \mid \xi_{\b u}(\lambda) \in \c O_0, \xi_{\b u}(\lambda) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } w(\b u) \rightarrow +\infty  \right\},
\]
then we define the map
\[
Sym^k \alpha_m: Sym^k_{\c O_0} \c C_0(\c O_0) \rightarrow Sym^k_{\c O_{0, p^m}} \c C_0(\c O_{0, p^m})
\]
as follows. Let
\begin{align*}
\alpha_m(\tilde \pi^{w(u)} x^u) &= \sum_{v \in M(f)} \mathcal{A}^m_{v, u}(\lambda) \tilde \pi^{w(v)} x^v \\
&= \sum_{v \in M(f)} \mathcal{A}^m_{v, u}(\lambda) E_v.
\end{align*}
We know from Section \ref{S: unit root formula} that 
\[
\mathcal{A}^m_{u,v} = \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), v \in M(f)} \tilde{\pi}^{(u)-w(v)} \mathcal{B}^m(\gamma, p^mv-u)\lambda^{\gamma}
\]
Then
\[
Sym^k \alpha_m(E_{u_{j_1}} E_{u_{j_2}} \cdots E_{u_{j_k}}) = \sum \mathcal{A}^m_{v_{l_1}, u_{j_1}}(\lambda) \cdots \mathcal{A}^m_{v_{l_k}, u_{j_k}}(\lambda) E_{v_{l_1}} \cdots E_{v_{l_k}},
\]
where the sum runs over all $v_{l_i} \in M(f)$ for each $i$, $1 \leq i \leq k$.
nodes.statement_short: The $k$-th symmetric power of $\mathcal C_0(\mathcal O_0)$ and the induced map $Sym^k\alpha_m$ via products of matrix entries $\mathcal A^m_{v,u}$.

nodes.name: Dual symmetric powers Sym^k C_0^*
nodes.statement:
We have as well a dual variant 
\[
Sym^k_{\c O_{0, p^m}} \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m}) := \{ \sum_{ |\b u| = k} A_{\b u}(\lambda) E_{\b u}^*\mid A_{\b u}(\lambda) \in \c O_{0, p^m} \}
\]
where we denote $E_u^* := \tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u}$ for each $u \in M(f)$, and using the linear order above write for each multiset $\b u = (u_{j_1}, \ldots, u_{j_k})$ of cardinality $k$ of indices, with $j_1 \leq \cdots \leq j_k$ we set $E_{\b u}^* := E_{u_1}^* \cdots E_{u_k}^*$.

nodes.name: Dual symmetric power map Sym^k(alpha_m^*)
nodes.statement:
Since $\alpha_m^*: \c C_{0}^*(\c O_{0, p^m}) \rightarrow \c C_{0}^*(\c O_{0, p^m})$, we may define for $\b u = (u_{j_1}, \ldots, u_{j_k})$,
\[
Sym^k(\alpha_m^*)(E_{\b u}^*) = \sum \mathcal{A}^*_{v_{l_1}, u_{j_1}}(\lambda) \mathcal{A}^*_{v_{l_2}, u_{j_2}}(\lambda) \cdots \mathcal{A}^*_{v_{l_k}, u_{j_k}}(\lambda) E_{\b v}^*
\]
where $\b v = (v_{l_1}, \ldots v_{l_k})$, the sum runs over $v_{l_i} \in \{ \tilde \pi^{- w(u)} x^{-u} \mid u \in M(f) \}$, and where $\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u}) = \sum_{v \in M(f)} \mathcal{A}^*_{u, v}(\lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}$.

nodes.name: Symmetric power pairing (.,.)_k
nodes.statement:
We extend the pairing above to these symmetric power spaces by ``linearly'' extending the following: for decomposable elements $\xi = \xi_1 \cdots \xi_k \in Sym^k_{\c O_{0, q_1}} \c C_0(\c O_{0, q_1})$ and $\xi^* = \xi_1^* \cdots \xi_k^* \in Sym^k_{\c O_{0, q_2}} \c C_0^*(\c O_{0, q_2})$,
\begin{equation} (\xi, \xi^*) := (\xi_1 \cdots \xi_k, \xi_1^* \cdots \xi_k^*)_k := \frac{1}{k!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_k} \prod_{i=1}^k (\xi_i, \xi_{\sigma(i)}^*),
\end{equation}
where $S_k$ denotes the symmetric group on $k$ letters.
nodes.statement_short: Pairing on $k$-th symmetric powers: symmetrized product of pairings of factors, divided by $k!$.

nodes.name: Symmetric pairing definition
nodes.statement: (\xi, \xi^*) := (\xi_1 \cdots \xi_k, \xi_1^* \cdots \xi_k^*)_k := \frac{1}{k!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_k} \prod_{i=1}^k (\xi_i, \xi_{\sigma(i)}^*),
nodes.label: E: sym pairing def

nodes.name: Duality of Sym^k alpha and Sym^k alpha^*
nodes.statement: (Sym^k \> \alpha_{a d(\bar t)} \xi, \xi^*)_k = (\xi, Sym^k \>\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* \xi^*)_k.
nodes.label: E: dual sym

nodes.name: Dual power series ring S_0^*(O_0)
nodes.statement: Denote by $\c S^*_0(\c O_0) := \c O_0[[ e_u^* : u \in M \setminus \{0\}]]$ the formal power series ring over $\c O_0$ in the variables $\{ e_u^* \}_{u \in M \setminus \{0\} }$, a set of formal symbols indexed by $M \setminus 0$.

nodes.name: Dual embedding Upsilon
nodes.statement: Using the same notation as before, define the embedding $\Upsilon: \c C_0^*(\c O_0) \hookrightarrow \c S_0^*(\c O_0)$ by $\Upsilon(\tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u}) := e_u^*$ for $u \in M \setminus \{ 0\}$, and $\Upsilon(1) := e_0^* = 1$.

nodes.name: Dual operator [alpha_m^*]_kappa
nodes.statement:
For $m \geq 1$,  we define the map $[\alpha_m^*]_\kappa: \c S_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m}) \rightarrow \c S_0^*({\c O}_{0, p^m})$ by 
\[
[\alpha_m^*]_\kappa( e_{u_1}^* \cdots e_{u_r}^* ) := (\Upsilon ( \alpha_m^*(1) ))^{\kappa - r} (\Upsilon ( \alpha_m^* (\tilde \pi^{-w(u_1)}\ x^{-u_1}) )) \cdots (\Upsilon ( \alpha_m^* (\tilde \pi^{-w(u_r)} x^{-u_r}))).
\]

nodes.name: Estimate (14) for [alpha_m^*]_kappa
nodes.statement: |[\alpha_m^*]_{\kappa}(e_{\b u}^*) | \leq |\tilde{\pi}^{(p-1)w(\b u)}|.
nodes.label: E: number14

nodes.name: Dual module O_{0,q}^*
nodes.statement:
Define the $R$ module
\[
\c O_{0, q}^* := \left\{ \zeta^* = \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} \zeta^*(\gamma) \tilde \pi^{- w_{q\Gamma}(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} \mid \zeta^*(\gamma) \in R \right\}.
\]

nodes.name: Projection pr_{M(Gamma)}
nodes.statement:
For series in $\lambda$, we define a projection (or truncation) map
\[
\text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)}: \quad
\sum_{\gamma \in \bb Z^s} A(\gamma) \lambda^{-\gamma} \longmapsto \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} A(\gamma) \lambda^{-\gamma}.
\]

nodes.name: Projection lands in O_{0,q}^*
nodes.statement: pr_{M(\Gamma)}( \xi \cdot \xi^*) \in \c O_{0, q}^*.
nodes.label: E: proj

nodes.name: Dual module S_0^*(O_0^*)
nodes.statement:
Define the $R$ module
\[
\c S_0^*(\c O_0^*) :=  \left\{ \omega^* = \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in \c S(M)} \omega^*(\gamma, \b u) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)}\lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^* \mid \omega^*(\gamma, \b u) \in R  \right\}
\]

nodes.name: Map Phi_lambda
nodes.statement: Define the map $\Phi_\lambda$ by $\lambda \mapsto \lambda^p$.

nodes.name: Dual operator beta^*_{kappa,t}
nodes.statement:
We define an $R$-linear map
\[
\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* := pr_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_\kappa \circ \Phi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)}
\]
by ``linearly'' extending over $R$ the action
\[
\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^*( \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^*) = pr_{M(\Gamma)}\left( \lambda^{-q_{\bar t} \gamma} \cdot [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_\kappa( e_{\b u}^*) \right).
\]

nodes.name: Lemma 4.2 (beta^* is an endomorphism)
nodes.statement: $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^*$ is an $R$-linear endomorphism of $\c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$.
conclusions: $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^*$ is an $R$-linear endomorphism of $\c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$
nodes.label: L: beta is endo

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement:
We have remarked already that $[\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_\kappa$ is a well-defined endomorphism of $\c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}})$. As such, we may write for each $\b u \in \c S(M)$,
\[
[ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_\kappa( e_{\b u}^*) = \sum_{\sigma \in M(\Gamma), \b v \in S(M)} B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \tilde \pi^{w_{q_{\bar t}\Gamma}(\sigma)} \lambda^\sigma e_{\b v}^* \in \c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}}),
\]
with $B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \in R$, $B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \rightarrow 0$ as $w_{q_{\bar t}\Gamma}(\sigma) + w(\b v) \rightarrow \infty$ using (\ref{E: number14}). For $\omega^* = \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} \omega^*(\gamma, \b u) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^* \in S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^*(\omega^*) &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)}\left( \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} \omega^*(\gamma, u) \tilde{\pi}^{-w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)}\lambda^{- q_{\bar t} \gamma} \cdot [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_\kappa (e_{\b u}^*) \right) \\
&= pr_{M(\Gamma)} \left( \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} \lambda^{- q_{\bar t} \gamma} \sum_{ \b u \in S(M)} \omega^*(\gamma, \b u) \sum_{\sigma \in M(\Gamma), \b v \in S(M)} B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \tilde \pi^{-w_{q_{\bar t} \Gamma}(\sigma)} \tilde{\pi}^{-w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)} \lambda^\sigma e_{\b v}^* \right) \\
&= \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma), \b v \in S(M)} C(\tau, \b v) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\tau)} \lambda^{-\tau} e_{\b v}^*,
\end{align*}
where
\[
C(\tau, \b v) := \sum_{\b u \in S(M)} \sum_{\substack{\gamma, \sigma \in M(\Gamma) \\ q_{\bar t} \gamma - \sigma = \tau}} \omega^*(\gamma, \b u) B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w_{q_{\bar t}\Gamma}(\sigma) + w_\Gamma(\tau)}.
\]
Observe that the exponent of $\tilde \pi$ satisfies
\[
-w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w_{q_{\bar t}\Gamma}(\sigma) + w_\Gamma(\tau) \geq \left( 1 - \frac{1}{q_{\bar t}} \right) w_\Gamma(\tau),
\]
so that the term $\tilde \pi^{- w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w_{q_{\bar t} \Gamma}(\sigma) + w_\Gamma(\tau)}$ is bounded in norm by 1 since $w(\tau) \geq 0$, and  $\omega^*(\gamma, \b u) \ \text{and} \  B_{\b u}(\sigma,v) \in R$. On the other hand, $B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \rightarrow 0$ as $w_\Gamma(\sigma) + w(\b v) \rightarrow \infty$ so that the coefficient $C(\tau, \b v)$ is defined, in $R$, and $\beta_\kappa^*( \omega^*) \in \c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$. Clearly it is $R$-linear.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $[\alpha^*]_\kappa$ on monomials using (14), compute the coefficients of $\beta^*(\omega^*)$, and bound the $\tilde\pi$-exponent below.

nodes.name: Recall [alpha^*]_kappa is an endomorphism
nodes.statement: We have remarked already that $[\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_\kappa$ is a well-defined endomorphism of $\c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}})$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall that $[\alpha^*]_\kappa$ is a well-defined endomorphism.

nodes.name: Expand on monomials
nodes.statement:
As such, we may write for each $\b u \in \c S(M)$,
\[
[ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_\kappa( e_{\b u}^*) = \sum_{\sigma \in M(\Gamma), \b v \in S(M)} B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \tilde \pi^{w_{q_{\bar t}\Gamma}(\sigma)} \lambda^\sigma e_{\b v}^* \in \c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}}),
\]
with $B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \in R$, $B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \rightarrow 0$ as $w_{q_{\bar t}\Gamma}(\sigma) + w(\b v) \rightarrow \infty$ using (\ref{E: number14}).
nodes.statement_short: Write its matrix coefficients, which tend to zero by (14).

nodes.name: Compute beta^*(omega^*)
nodes.statement:
For $\omega^* = \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} \omega^*(\gamma, \b u) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^* \in S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^*(\omega^*) &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)}\left( \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} \omega^*(\gamma, u) \tilde{\pi}^{-w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)}\lambda^{- q_{\bar t} \gamma} \cdot [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_\kappa (e_{\b u}^*) \right) \\
&= pr_{M(\Gamma)} \left( \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} \lambda^{- q_{\bar t} \gamma} \sum_{ \b u \in S(M)} \omega^*(\gamma, \b u) \sum_{\sigma \in M(\Gamma), \b v \in S(M)} B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \tilde \pi^{-w_{q_{\bar t} \Gamma}(\sigma)} \tilde{\pi}^{-w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)} \lambda^\sigma e_{\b v}^* \right) \\
&= \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma), \b v \in S(M)} C(\tau, \b v) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\tau)} \lambda^{-\tau} e_{\b v}^*,
\end{align*}
where
\[
C(\tau, \b v) := \sum_{\b u \in S(M)} \sum_{\substack{\gamma, \sigma \in M(\Gamma) \\ q_{\bar t} \gamma - \sigma = \tau}} \omega^*(\gamma, \b u) B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w_{q_{\bar t}\Gamma}(\sigma) + w_\Gamma(\tau)}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\beta^*(\omega^*)$ and its coefficients $C(\tau,\mathbf v)$.

nodes.name: Bound the exponent of pi-tilde
nodes.statement:
Observe that the exponent of $\tilde \pi$ satisfies
\[
-w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w_{q_{\bar t}\Gamma}(\sigma) + w_\Gamma(\tau) \geq \left( 1 - \frac{1}{q_{\bar t}} \right) w_\Gamma(\tau),
\]
so that the term $\tilde \pi^{- w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w_{q_{\bar t} \Gamma}(\sigma) + w_\Gamma(\tau)}$ is bounded in norm by 1 since $w(\tau) \geq 0$, and  $\omega^*(\gamma, \b u) \ \text{and} \  B_{\b u}(\sigma,v) \in R$.
nodes.statement_short: The $\tilde\pi$-exponent is nonnegative, so terms are bounded by 1.

nodes.name: Coefficients converge; conclude
nodes.statement: On the other hand, $B_{\b u}(\sigma, \b v) \rightarrow 0$ as $w_\Gamma(\sigma) + w(\b v) \rightarrow \infty$ so that the coefficient $C(\tau, \b v)$ is defined, in $R$, and $\beta_\kappa^*( \omega^*) \in \c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$. Clearly it is $R$-linear.
nodes.statement_short: Coefficients converge in $R$, so $\beta^*$ is an $R$-linear endomorphism.

nodes.name: Length of an element
nodes.statement: For $\xi \in \c S_0(\c O_0)$, define $\text{length}(\xi)$ as the supremum of the lengths of the monomials $e_{\b u}$ in the support of $\xi$ (i.e. those terms appearing with non-zero coefficients).

nodes.name: Truncated space S_0^{(k)}(O_0)
nodes.statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer. Define $\c S_0^{(k)}(\c O_0) := \{ \xi \in \c S_0(\c O_0) \mid \text{length}(\xi) \leq k \}$.

nodes.name: Pairing <.,.>_k
nodes.statement:
We now work over $R$ and define a new pairing $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_k: \c S_0^{(k)}(\c O_0) \times \c S_0^{*(k)}(\c O_0^*) \rightarrow \Omega$ as follows. (Here again $\c S_0^{*(k)}(\c O_0^*)$ is the $R$-submodule of $\c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$ of series with support in monomials of degree $\leq k$, namely $\{ e_{\b u}^* \mid |\b u| \leq k \}$, with coefficients in $\c O_0^*$.) Let $\xi := \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} \xi(\gamma, \b u) \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u} \in  \c S_0^{(k)}(\c O_0)$, and $\xi^* := \sum_{\sigma \in M(\Gamma), \b v \in S(M)} \xi^*(\sigma, \b v) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\sigma)} \lambda^{-\sigma} e_{\b v}^* \in \c S_0^{*(k)}(\c O_0^*)$, set
\[
\langle \xi, \xi^* \rangle_k := \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} \xi(\gamma, \b u) \xi^*(\gamma, \b u) (e_{\b u}, e_{\b u}^*)_k,
\]
where $(\cdot, \cdot)_k$ was defined above.

nodes.name: Approximating integers k_m
nodes.statement: Let $k_m$ be a sequence of positive integers which tend to infinity (in the usual archimedean sense) and such that $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} k_m = \kappa$ $p$-adically.

nodes.name: Truncated Frobenius [alpha]_{(kappa;m)}
nodes.statement_short: Extend the $k_m$-th symmetric power Frobenius by zero on monomials of length $>k_m$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.3 (truncated Frobenius converges)
nodes.statement: $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)} ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa$ as maps from $\c S_0(\c O_0) \rightarrow \c S_0(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}})$.
conclusions: $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)} ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa$ as maps from $\c S_0(\c O_0) \rightarrow \c S_0(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}})$
nodes.statement_short: The truncated symmetric-power Frobenius maps converge to $[\alpha_{ad(\bar t)}]_\kappa$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement:
Write
\begin{equation} \left( [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa \right) (e_{u_1} e_{u_2} \cdots e_{u_r} ) = \left( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - r} - \Upsilon( \alpha_{ a d(\bar t)}(1))^{\kappa - r} \right) ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_1)} x^{u_1} ))) \cdots ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_r)} x^{u_r} ))).
\end{equation}
If $r \leq k_m$, then the first factor on the right may itself be factored into
\[
-\Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{\kappa - r} (1 - (\Upsilon(\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - \kappa}).
\]
Writing $\kappa = k_m + p^{\tau(m)} \sigma_m$ (with $\tau(m) \rightarrow \infty$ and $\sigma_m \in \bb Z_p$) then
\[
| 1 - (\Upsilon(\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - \kappa} | \leq | \tilde \pi^{\tau(m) + 1} |
\]
as in the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.2]{MR3249829}, and using the estimate (\ref{E: upsilon estimate}). If $r > k_m$ then (\ref{E: double star}) becomes
\begin{align*}
\left( [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa \right) (e_{\b u} ) = -[\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa e_{\b u} = - \Upsilon( \alpha_{ a d(\bar t)}(1))^{\kappa - r} ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_1)} x^{u_1} ))) \cdots ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_r)} x^{u_r} )))
\end{align*}
so that focussing on the $r$ rightmost factors,
\[
\left|   \left( [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa \right) e_{\b u} \right| \leq |\tilde \pi|^{\frac{p^{a d(\bar t) - 1} - 1}{p-1} \frac{1}{p^{a d(\bar t) - 1}} w(\b u)}
\]
coming from (\ref{E: upsilon estimate}). But  $w(\b u) \geq r w_0 > k_m w_0$ (where $w_0 := \min \{ w(\b u) \mid \b u \in M(f) \setminus \{0\} \}$). In terms of the operator norm,
\[
\|  [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} \| \leq | \tilde \pi |^{\min \left\{ \tau(m) + 1, \frac{p^{a d(\bar t) -1} - 1}{p-1} \frac{1}{p^{a d(\bar t) -1}} k_m w_0 \right\} }.
\]
As $k_m$ and $\tau(m)$ both tend to infinity as $m$ grows, we see that  $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)} ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa$.
nodes.statement_short: Split by monomial length $r\le k_m$ vs $r>k_m$; bound the difference by $p$-adic closeness $k_m\to\kappa$ or by the weight estimate (8). Combine into an operator-norm bound tending to 0.

nodes.name: Write the difference
nodes.statement_short: Write the difference of the two maps on a monomial.

nodes.name: Case r <= k_m
nodes.statement:
If $r \leq k_m$, then the first factor on the right may itself be factored into
\[
-\Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{\kappa - r} (1 - (\Upsilon(\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - \kappa}).
\]
Writing $\kappa = k_m + p^{\tau(m)} \sigma_m$ (with $\tau(m) \rightarrow \infty$ and $\sigma_m \in \bb Z_p$) then
\[
| 1 - (\Upsilon(\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - \kappa} | \leq | \tilde \pi^{\tau(m) + 1} |
\]
as in the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.2]{MR3249829}, and using the estimate (\ref{E: upsilon estimate}).
nodes.statement_short: For $r\le k_m$, the first factor is small since $k_m\to\kappa$ $p$-adically.

nodes.name: Case r > k_m
nodes.statement_short: For $r>k_m$, the weight estimate (8) bounds the term by a power of $\tilde\pi$ growing with $k_m$.

nodes.name: Operator norm bound
nodes.statement:
In terms of the operator norm,
\[
\|  [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} \| \leq | \tilde \pi |^{\min \left\{ \tau(m) + 1, \frac{p^{a d(\bar t) -1} - 1}{p-1} \frac{1}{p^{a d(\bar t) -1}} k_m w_0 \right\} }.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine into an operator-norm bound.

nodes.name: Conclude convergence
nodes.statement: As $k_m$ and $\tau(m)$ both tend to infinity as $m$ grows, we see that  $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)} ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa$.
nodes.statement_short: Both exponents tend to infinity, giving convergence.

nodes.name: Difference of truncated and full Frobenius
nodes.statement: \left( [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa \right) (e_{u_1} e_{u_2} \cdots e_{u_r} ) = \left( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - r} - \Upsilon( \alpha_{ a d(\bar t)}(1))^{\kappa - r} \right) ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_1)} x^{u_1} ))) \cdots ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_r)} x^{u_r} ))).
nodes.label: E: double star

nodes.name: Argument for convergence of dual truncated Frobenius
nodes.statement:
In an altogether similar manner, we have by Lemma \ref{L: better conv}, for $u \not= 0$, $\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u})$ belongs to $\c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m})$, and (recalling (\ref{E: an estimate}))
\[
| \alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u}) | \leq | \tilde \pi |^{(p-1) w(u)}.
\]
Also $\alpha_m^*(1) = 1 + \eta^*(\lambda)$ with $\eta^*(\lambda) \in \c O_{0, p^m}$ and $|\eta^*(\lambda)| \leq |\tilde \pi|$.
nodes.statement_short: Analogue of the proof of Lemma 4.3, using Lemma 4.1's estimate (10) and $\alpha_m^*(1)=1+O(\tilde\pi)$.

nodes.name: Convergence of dual truncated Frobenius
nodes.statement:
With these observations, an entirely similar argument shows 
$\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_\kappa$ as maps from $\c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}}) \rightarrow \c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}}) $.
conclusions: $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_\kappa$

nodes.name: Truncated operators beta_{(kappa;m)} and beta^*_{(kappa;m)}
Limits of truncated beta and beta^*
nodes.statement:
\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} &= \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} \\
\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* &= \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^*. \notag
nodes.label: E: beta limit

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4 (adjointness of truncated operators)
conclusions:
\label{E: pairing with estimate}
\langle \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} = \langle \xi, \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* \xi^* \rangle_{k_m}.
nodes.statement_short: $\beta_{(\kappa;m)}$ and $\beta^*_{(\kappa;m)}$ are adjoint for $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{k_m}$.

nodes.name: Adjointness identity (18)
nodes.statement: \langle \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} = \langle \xi, \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* \xi^* \rangle_{k_m}.
nodes.label: E: pairing with estimate

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement_short: Reduce by linearity to monomials and compute both sides as the same constant-term coefficient, using the symmetric-power duality (13).

nodes.name: Rewrite symmetric-power duality
nodes.statement_short: Restate duality (13) for the truncated maps as (19).

nodes.name: Reduce to monomials
nodes.statement:
Next, by linearity we only need consider $\xi = \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}$ and $\xi^* = \lambda^{-\sigma} e_{\b v}^*$ where $\gamma, \sigma \in M(\Gamma)$ and $\b u, \b v \in S(M)$. We may write
\[
(e_{\b u}, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} = \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma)} C(\tau) \lambda^\tau.
\]
nodes.statement_short: By linearity, reduce to monomials and name the coefficients $C(\tau)$.

nodes.name: psi_lambda and Phi_lambda are adjoint
nodes.statement:
Next, observe that
\[
\langle \psi_\lambda \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} = \langle \xi, \Phi_\lambda \xi^* \rangle_{k_m}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: $\psi_\lambda$ and $\Phi_\lambda$ are adjoint.

nodes.name: Compute left side
nodes.statement_short: Left side equals $C(q_{\bar t}\sigma-\gamma)$ or 0.

nodes.name: Compute right side and conclude
nodes.statement_short: Right side gives the same value.

nodes.name: Truncated duality (19)
nodes.statement: ( [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa, m)} \xi, \xi^*)_{k_m} = (\xi,  [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} \xi^*)_{k_m}.
nodes.label: E: rewrite duality

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.5
nodes.statement:
Observe that $\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ and $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}$ are completely continuous operators on the $p$-adic Banach $R$-algebra $\c S_0(\c O_0)$ (viewed as $R$-algebra) with orthonormal basis $\{ \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u} \mid \gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M) \}$. Let $\c T_0(R) \ \text{be} \ \c S_0(\c O_0)$ viewed in this way as $R$-algebra. Similarly, write $\c T_0^*(R)$ for the $b(I)$-space (over $R$) in Serre's terminology with ``basis'' $I := \{ \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^* \mid \gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M) \}$ with coefficients in $R$. Again, $\c T_0^*(R)$ is just $\c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$ viewed over $R$. Then
\[
\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T) = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T).
\]

Similarly, $\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ is a continuous $R$-linear endomorphism of $\c T_0^*(R)$ to itself. We may consider a matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ with entries in $R$ defined by
\[
\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}( \tilde \pi^{-w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^*) = \sum \f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}_{(\delta, \b v), (\gamma, \b u)} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\delta)} \lambda^{-\delta} e_{\b v}^*.
\]
Using the matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$, we define in the usual way the Fredholm determinant $det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* T) = \sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^*) T^j$ where $C_0  = 1$ and $C_j$ is the series of all principal $j \times j$ subdeterminants of the matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$. The $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_{k_m}$-adjointness of $\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ and $\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ implies $C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}) = C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^*)$, so that
\[
det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* T) = det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T).
\]
The uniform convergence $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}  =: \f B^*_{\kappa, \bar t}$  over the entries implies that the series $\sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\f B_{\kappa, \bar t}^*) T^j$ is well-defined, and is the coefficient-wise limit  of $det(1 - \f B^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T)$ as $m \rightarrow \infty$. If we then define
\[
det(1 - \beta^*_{\kappa, \bar t} T) := \sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\f B_{\kappa, \bar t}^*) T^j,
\]
then we have shown:
nodes.statement_short: Approximate by truncated operators: adjointness (Lemma 4.4) equates their Fredholm determinants, and the limits (17) pass to $\beta$ and $\beta^*$.

nodes.name: View operators over R
nodes.statement: Observe that $\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ and $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}$ are completely continuous operators on the $p$-adic Banach $R$-algebra $\c S_0(\c O_0)$ (viewed as $R$-algebra) with orthonormal basis $\{ \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u} \mid \gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M) \}$. Let $\c T_0(R) \ \text{be} \ \c S_0(\c O_0)$ viewed in this way as $R$-algebra. Similarly, write $\c T_0^*(R)$ for the $b(I)$-space (over $R$) in Serre's terminology with ``basis'' $I := \{ \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^* \mid \gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M) \}$ with coefficients in $R$. Again, $\c T_0^*(R)$ is just $\c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$ viewed over $R$.
nodes.statement_short: View $\mathcal S_0(\mathcal O_0)$ and its dual as Banach/$b(I)$ spaces $\mathcal T_0(R)$, $\mathcal T_0^*(R)$ over $R$.

nodes.name: Limit of Fredholm determinants of beta
nodes.statement:
Then
\[
\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T) = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Determinants of $\beta_{(\kappa;m)}$ converge to that of $\beta$.

nodes.name: Matrix of beta^*_{(kappa;m)}
nodes.statement:
Similarly, $\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ is a continuous $R$-linear endomorphism of $\c T_0^*(R)$ to itself. We may consider a matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ with entries in $R$ defined by
\[
\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}( \tilde \pi^{-w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^*) = \sum \f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}_{(\delta, \b v), (\gamma, \b u)} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\delta)} \lambda^{-\delta} e_{\b v}^*.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the matrix of $\beta^*_{(\kappa;m)}$.

nodes.name: Fredholm determinant of beta^*_{(kappa;m)}
nodes.statement: Using the matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$, we define in the usual way the Fredholm determinant $det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* T) = \sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^*) T^j$ where $C_0  = 1$ and $C_j$ is the series of all principal $j \times j$ subdeterminants of the matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define its Fredholm determinant via principal minors.

nodes.name: Adjointness equates determinants
nodes.statement:
The $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_{k_m}$-adjointness of $\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ and $\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ implies $C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}) = C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^*)$, so that
\[
det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* T) = det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Adjointness gives equal principal-minor sums, so equal determinants.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit for beta^*
nodes.statement: The uniform convergence $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}  =: \f B^*_{\kappa, \bar t}$  over the entries implies that the series $\sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\f B_{\kappa, \bar t}^*) T^j$ is well-defined, and is the coefficient-wise limit  of $det(1 - \f B^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T)$ as $m \rightarrow \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform convergence of matrices gives a limiting determinant.

nodes.name: Define det(1 - beta^* T) and conclude
nodes.statement:
If we then define
\[
det(1 - \beta^*_{\kappa, \bar t} T) := \sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\f B_{\kappa, \bar t}^*) T^j,
\]
then we have shown:
nodes.statement_short: Define $det(1-\beta^*T)$ as the limit; the theorem follows.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.5 (dual Fredholm determinant)
conclusions: $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T) = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* T)$

\label{E: L0  and dual}
L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* T)^{\delta_{q_{\bar t}}^{s}}.
nodes.statement_short: $\beta$ and $\beta^*$ have the same Fredholm determinant, so $L^{(0)}$ is expressed via $\beta^*$.

nodes.name: L^{(0)} via dual operator
nodes.statement: L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* T)^{\delta_{q_{\bar t}}^{s}}.
nodes.label: E: L0  and dual

nodes.name: Generic total family H(Lambda, lambda, x)
nodes.statement:
We now replace every coefficient of $G$ (w.r.t the variables $x$ and $\lambda$) with a new variable $\Lambda$: set $ \b f(\Lambda,x)=\sum_{u \in Supp(f)} \Lambda_u x^u \ \text{and} \ \c P(\Lambda, \lambda. x) = \sum_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)} \Lambda_{\gamma, v} \lambda^\gamma x^v$ and
\[
H(\Lambda, \lambda, x) := \b f(\Lambda,x)  +  \c P(\Lambda, \lambda. x) .
\]

nodes.name: Newton polytope of H
nodes.statement: As before, let $\Delta_{\infty}(H)$ denote the Newton polytope at infinity in $\bb R^{s+n}$ of $H$ (in $\lambda$ and $x$ variables).

nodes.name: Cone(H) and monoid M(H)
nodes.statement: Let $Cone(H)$ be the cone in $\bb R^{s+n}$ over $\Delta_{\infty}(H)$ and $M(H) = Cone(H) \cap \bb Z^{s+n}$ be the relevant monoid.

nodes.name: Weight w_H dominates total weight
nodes.statement:
By our hypothesis that the $x$-support of $P$ is contained in $\Delta_{\infty}(f)$ we have the polyhedral weight function on this polytope $w_H$ dominates the total weight $w_{\text{tot}} := w_{\Gamma} + w_f$ relative to the polyhedron $\Gamma \times \Delta_{\infty}$; more precisely 
\[
w_{\text{tot}}(\gamma, u) \leq w_H(\gamma, u)
\]
for all $(\gamma, u) \in M(H)$.
conclusions: w_{\text{tot}}(\gamma, u) \leq w_H(\gamma, u)
nodes.statement_short: The polyhedral weight $w_H$ of $H$ dominates $w_{tot}=w_\Gamma+w_f$.

nodes.name: Rings K and K_0
nodes.statement:
We define $\c K := R[[\Lambda]]$ and 
\[
\c K_0 := \{ \xi \in \sum_{v \in \bb Z_{\geq 0}^t} \xi_v \Lambda^v \in \c K \mid \xi_v \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } v \rightarrow \infty \},
\]
where $t$ is the cardinality of $\{ Supp(f) \} \cup \{ Supp(P) \}$.

nodes.name: Spaces W(K_0) and W_0(K_0)
Spaces D(W(K_0)) and D_0(W_0(K_0))
Modules S_0^*(W(K_0)) and S_0^*(W_0(K_0))
nodes.statement:
We define a $\c K_0$-module
\[
\c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0)) := \{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} A_{\gamma, \b u}(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^* \mid A_{\gamma, \b u} \in \c K_0 \}.
\]
and a $\c W_0(\c K_0)$-algebra
\[
\c S^*_0(\c W_0(\c K_0)) := \{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} \xi^*_{ \b u}(\Lambda, \lambda) e_{\b u}^* \mid \xi^*_{ \b u}(\Lambda, \lambda) \in \c W_0(K_0) \}.
\]

nodes.name: Relative Frobenius F(Lambda, lambda, x)
nodes.statement:
We define a relative Frobenius map as follows. First, set
\begin{align*}
F(\Lambda, \lambda, x) &:= \prod_{u \in Supp(f)} \theta(\Lambda_u x^u) \cdot \prod_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)} \theta( \Lambda_{\gamma, v} \lambda^\gamma x^v) \\
F_m(\Lambda, \lambda, x) &:= \prod_{i=0}^{m-1} F(\Lambda^{p^i}, \lambda^{p^i}, x^{p^i}),
\end{align*}
and note that, similar to before,
\[
F_m(\Lambda, \lambda, x) = \sum_{(\gamma, u) \in M(H)} \c F^m_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \lambda^{\gamma} x^u 
\]
with $\c F^m_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda)= B_{\gamma,u}(\Lambda) \tilde{\pi}^{w_{tot}(\gamma,u)/p^{m-1}} = \b B_{\gamma,u}(\Lambda) \tilde{\pi}^{w_H(\gamma,u)/p^{m-1}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Relative Frobenius $F(\Lambda,\lambda,x)$: product of splitting functions with the coefficients as variables $\Lambda$, and its iterate $F_m$.

nodes.name: Relative dual Frobenius alpha^*_{m,Lambda} is well-defined
nodes.statement:
It follows that, if we set (as before)
\[
\alpha_m^*(\Lambda, \lambda) := \text{pr}_{M(f)} \circ F_m(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \circ \Phi_x^m,
\]
where $\Phi_x$ sends $x^u \mapsto x^{pu}$ and $\text{pr}_{M(f)}$ was defined above, then an argument similar to Lemma \ref{L: better conv} shows
\[
\alpha_{m, \Lambda}^*: \c D_0(\c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)) \rightarrow \c D_0(\c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)),
\]
where $\c W_{0, p^m}$ is defined by replacing $\tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma}$ with $\tilde \pi^{w_{p^m \Gamma}}$ in the definition of $\c W_0$. Furthermore, 
\[
\alpha_{m, \Lambda}^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}) = \sum_{u \in M(f)} C_{u, v}(\Lambda, \gamma) \tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u}
\]
with $C_{u, v}(\Lambda, \lambda) \in \c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)$ and $C_{u, v}(\Lambda, \lambda) \rightarrow 0$ as $w(u) \rightarrow \infty$.
conclusions: \alpha_{m, \Lambda}^*: \c D_0(\c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)) \rightarrow \c D_0(\c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)),
nodes.statement_short: Analogue of Lemma 4.1 over $\mathcal K_0$: $\alpha^*_{m,\Lambda}$ preserves $\mathcal D_0(\mathcal W_{0,p^m}(\mathcal K_0))$ with decaying coefficients.

nodes.name: Operator [alpha^*_m]_kappa over K_0
nodes.statement: For any $\kappa \in \bb{Z}_p$, we define $[\alpha^*_m]_{\kappa} : \c S^*_{0,p^m}(\c W_0(\c K_0)) \rightarrow \c S^*_{0,p^m}(\c W_0(\c K_0))$ using (\ref{E: number14}).

nodes.name: beta^*_{kappa,t,Lambda} is a K_0-endomorphism
nodes.statement:
By an argument similar to Lemma \ref{L: beta is endo}, the map
\[
\beta_{\kappa, \bar t, \Lambda}^*: \c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0)) \rightarrow \c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0))
\]
defined by 
\[
\beta_{\kappa, \bar t, \Lambda}^* := \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_\kappa  \circ \Phi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)}.
\]
is an endomorphism over $\c K_0$.
conclusions: is an endomorphism over $\c K_0$

nodes.name: Units M_0(Gamma), M_0(f), M_0(H)
nodes.statement: Set $M_0(\Gamma) = M(\Gamma) \cap (- M(\Gamma)), M_0(f) = M(f) \cap (- M(f)), \ \text{and} \ M_0(H) = M(H) \cap (-M(H))$.

nodes.name: Projection pr_0
nodes.statement:
Define the projection map 
\[
\text{pr}_0: \quad  \sum_{\gamma \in \bb Z^s, u \in \bb Z^n} C(\gamma, u) \lambda^\gamma x^u \longmapsto \sum_{\gamma \in M_0(\Gamma), u \in M_0(f)} C(\gamma, u) \lambda^\gamma x^u.
\]

nodes.name: Coefficients A_{gamma,u}(Lambda)
